case-a.summary: Benign office activity. Identity, endpoint, and network agree.

case-b.likely_story: Suspicious execution and outbound traffic on an already authenticated session. Identity evidence does not by itself prove credential theft.
case-b.summary: Endpoint and network are suspicious; identity looks normal. Agents should disagree on account takeover vs session-based activity.

case-c.likely_story: Identity-led: geographically implausible second login. Endpoint/network on USER-PC stay quiet, so the story is not the same as case-b.
case-c.summary: Impossible-travel pattern. Specialists will not all tell the same story.

case-d.summary: Repeated HTTPS is a signed-looking corporate updater to an allowlisted address. Specialists should agree this is benign.

case-e.likely_story: One connection to an address with no intel record, from Chrome, after a normal office login. Do not name a malware family. Confidence stays limited.
case-e.summary: Network is mildly unusual. Endpoint and intel do not corroborate. The report must stay uncertain.
